title: design-map
description: In-repo manifest linking code components to design references for sources without a machine link (Stitch, Claude Design) or as an override for Figma.

tokens.description: Design-name to code-name token aliases, keyed by code token name. Lets token-compliance match tokens whose design and code vocabularies differ (e.g. code 'onSurface' <-> design 'color/on-surface').

aliasGroup.description: Code token name -> design token name.

refVariant.description: A reference handle tagged with the variant slot (state/theme/size) it fills.

previewIdVariant.description: A candidate preview id tagged with the variant slot (state/theme/size) it fills. The candidate-side mirror of refVariant: lets one code component bind several previews when each theme/state/size is authored as its own @Preview. See design-parity issue #111.

knownDifferenceScope.description: Exact compose-preview-known-differences/v1 locator for one visual pair. The current reference hash is computed from the bytes being diffed, never configured here.

ref.description: Source-specific reference handle(s). A string binds a single node. A list of variant-tagged handles binds several nodes (a screen's states/themes/sizes in separate frames). Figma: 'figma:<fileKey>/<nodeId>'. Stitch: 'stitch:<designId>'. Claude Design: repo-relative path to a committed HTML export, a '.json' DTCG token artifact, or a 'live:<path>' prototype the adapter live-renders per viewport instead of rasterizing a static export (issue #85). Bundle: repo-relative path to a committed directory or '.zip' of reference PNGs plus a manifest.json.

refSet.description: Optional handle for the component FAMILY that `ref` is one variant of — a Figma component set, or whatever the source calls the node owning a component's variants. Sources without the concept omit it. Kept separate from `ref` because the two serve different consumers: parity diffs against `ref`, so that must be one concrete renderable variant, while whole-screen matching (page backdrops) sees an instance reporting its own variant plus its set, and a screen rarely uses the exact variant a catalog pictured. Figma: 'figma:<fileKey>/<nodeId>' naming a COMPONENT_SET.

referenceContentsOnly.description: Whether a Figma export includes only the mapped node's own content. Defaults true. Set false only when this reference intentionally relies on overlapping sheet layers such as an authored backdrop.

previewId.description: Optional compose-ai-tools preview id this code handle renders as. A string binds a single candidate preview (e.g. 'ee.app.FooKt.Bar'); a list of variant-tagged handles binds several themes/states/sizes authored as separate @Previews, each re-tagged onto its variant slot and merged into one candidate (issue #111). Links a preview-bundle/daemon candidate (keyed by preview id) to this reference (keyed by code handle). See design-parity issues #44 and #111.

tokensFile.description: Optional repo-relative path to a committed W3C DTCG token file whose tokens are this component's spec tokens. Populates the reference's tokens for sources that don't expose them (bundle, claude-design) or overrides what an adapter resolved. See design-parity issues #89 and #87.

density.description: Optional scale of the reference artwork: source pixels per density-independent pixel. A board drawn at 3x is 3. Lets a consumer quote the design's spacing and type in the same dp/sp the code side resolves, instead of naming the board's own pixel unit and leaving the reader to guess whether 'text 31.5px' and 'bodyMedium 14sp' agree (design-parity issue #279). Omit when unknown — a wrong factor silently rescales every spec, which is worse than a stated px.

knownDifferences.description: Exact known-difference locator scopes keyed by state/theme/size visual key. Kept per component so common keys such as default/light cannot collide across a run.
